sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: FLAG-tagged WT TrIP was expressed on the cell surface (anti-FLAG flow cytometry) and used in T-cell stimulation assays (α-CD3/CD28 stimulation, GFP-gated time-course analysis in D10 T cells; PMC6279406 Fig. 1B–D). Function of the tagged construct was assessed and the protein retained its inhibitory role in T-cell activation, consistent with surface_and_function.
sites.rationale: PIK3IP1 is a single-pass type I transmembrane protein with signal peptide 1–21 and a large extracellular domain spanning residues 22–170. L7 explicitly states the FLAG tag is placed at the N-terminus of the mature extracellular stalk, and because there is exactly one extracellular terminus (the mature N-terminus after SP cleavage), the junction is unambiguously after residue 21 (G) and before residue 22 (S). Python verification confirms res(21)=G and res(22)=S, with 149 residues separating the tag from the TM boundary (171), well above the ≥3-residue minimum. L1–L4 further demonstrate that this N-terminally FLAG-tagged construct retains surface expression and participates in functional T-cell stimulation assays. Full-length murine and human PIK3IP1 (TrIP) constructs bearing an N-terminal FLAG tag were transiently expressed in D10 T cells (PMC6279406, L1–L4) and HEK293T cells (PMC11615590, L5–L7). L7 explicitly describes 'an N-terminal Flag-tag on the stalk' of the full-length transmembrane protein. PIK3IP1 has a single-pass type I topology with signal peptide residues 1–21 and exactly one extracellular terminus (mature N-terminus at residue 22); the FLAG tag must reside after SP cleavage at residue 21. Surface display was confirmed by anti-FLAG flow cytometry in all studies.

sources.claim: To test this, we compared binding of the Ab’s to full-length TrIP versus a construct engineered to lack the kringle domain, but still bearing an N-terminal Flag-tag on the stalk for detection.

literature_notes: All seven Flag-tag ledger lines (L1–L7) converge on the same N-terminal extracellular site; no ledger line pins a second distinct extracellular junction or names a residue number, so only one site is reported. The C-terminal Myc/6His tag (L8–L9) is intracellular and is recorded in other_positions. No internal loop insertion is supported by the ledger.

literature_other_positions.note: pEF1MycHisA adds C-terminal Myc and 6His tags after residue 263, which lies in the intracellular domain (192–263); detected by anti-Myc antibody, not by surface staining — not a surface tag site.
